channel.title: News Officina
channel.description: Independent. These outlets are written with AI from public sources; one editor reads and approves what goes out. Each says how it is made on its own About page.

item.title: Europa Surgit: No settlement signed without Europe in the chair
item.description: Moscow refused to widen the talks, so our defence must not be settled in a phone call. Back the one seat we have already chosen: ceasefire first, then a settlement Europe endorses only because it was in the room.

item.title: Europae Laeva: Slovakia and France team up to push for power bills decoupled from gas prices
item.description: President Peter Pellegrini called the EU's gas-linked pricing illogical for a country that does not depend on gas for its electricity. The visit also brought a 120 million euro helicopter deal and talks on defence cooperation.

item.title: Europa Surgit: Independence Day march fills Warsaw as crowd size stays disputed
item.description: Warsaw city hall put the turnout at about 250,000, organisers at up to one million, as flares and firecrackers defied a city ban. Police secured more than 450 pyrotechnic items across the route.

item.title: Europa Surgit: Nuclear power should set its own price, not carry the price of gas
item.description: Slovakia and France want European electricity pricing reformed, and they are right. When your reactors are cheaper than everyone's gas, your bill should show it.

item.title: Europa Surgit: The Nordics wrote Europe's defence blueprint. Copy it, all of it
item.description: Sweden's record spending still leaves NATO's capability targets unmet, and money alone will not close the gap. Only a binding legal framework for joint procurement and shared planning can, so the EU should build one modelled on the Nordic agreement.

item.title: Europae Dexter: Sweden's defence plan must survive an America that leaves
item.description: Even with the Americans in, Sweden's Army and Air Force miss NATO's capability targets. A defence built on forces no Swedish minister controls is not a plan, it is a bet.

item.title: Europae Laeva: Nordic ministers to develop joint defence agreement as Sweden borrows SEK 300bn
item.description: The planned agreement would give Nordic defence cooperation a legal footing, while DN reports Sweden's record defence funding still falls short of Nato targets. From 1 January 2027, conscripts up to 47 can be called back for standby or war service.

item.title: Leo Batavus: Nordic defence ministers agree to develop a joint defence agreement
item.description: The decision of 12 November 2026 would give the Nordic defence cooperation a legal framework. Separately, the Riksdag voted to raise the military service age limit to 47, effective 1 January 2027.

item.title: Europae Dexter: Kremlin tells Witkoff and Kushner Russia is ready to redesign European security now
item.description: The Kremlin says it wants European support for a new security architecture, yet keeps European envoys out of the Ukraine talks. Moscow and Kyiv also disagree on whether a ceasefire or a continental settlement comes first.

item.title: Europae Dexter: Zelenskyy gives EU until November to decide who speaks for Europe in war-end talks
item.description: Politico reports EU leaders meeting in Dublin are split among candidates for the role, while the Washington Post says Russia has resisted any European place at the table.

item.title: Nuntii Europae: Slovak and French presidents call for overhaul of EU electricity pricing
item.description: Peter Pellegrini and Emmanuel Macron met in Paris for their first bilateral talks, with a 120 million euro contract for three Airbus helicopters signed in the days around the meeting.

item.title: Europae Dexter: Europe must pay for the army Moscow wants bargained away
item.description: While Bulgaria and Slovakia refuse the package, the size of Europe's second-largest army on the continent is being settled in Abu Dhabi without us. Fund it now, every state contributing, or lose the seat at the table.

item.title: Europae Dexter: Europe has decided to leave Palantir. It has not yet built what comes next.
item.description: Spain, the United Kingdom and Germany have moved to end their dependence on Palantir, while NATO still runs the Palantir-derived system it chose when no European alternative existed. The Bundeswehr is testing about thirty European candidates, but no replacement is in service: sovereignty on this layer is a decision taken, not a capacity confirmed.

item.title: Nuntii Europae: EU leaders gather in Dublin to debate who speaks for Europe in Ukraine talks
item.description: The debate, called at Italy's request, will not produce a name before December. Poland objects to western Europe negotiating over the east, while Estonia says the existing envoys are enough.

item.title: Europa Surgit: Fake bomb threats hit schools across Italy, Scotland and Ireland
item.description: Police in each country judged the emailed warnings not credible, and investigators are tracing the messages to a hacked university account in Taiwan.

item.title: Europae Laeva: Guterres urges windfall tax on oil giants, cites $600 million climate fund
item.description: The UN Secretary-General told COP31 leaders that nine oil companies made $95 billion in profits last quarter, while the Loss and Damage Fund has received $600 million. He said it is time to make polluters pay.

item.title: Nuntii Europae: US Treasury Secretary moves to military base after death threats linked to Iran
item.description: The United States has also moved refuelling aircraft from a British air base to Germany and other locations, and charged three men accused of plotting an attack on another British base on behalf of Iran's Revolutionary Guard.

item.title: Europae Laeva: Europe guards its ministries and leaves its food to hackers
item.description: The state intercepted 3.5 million malicious emails for the foreign ministry while supermarkets were broken into through open doors the government itself named. We pay twice, in spoiled food and in fear.

item.title: Europa Patriarum: France blames Iran's Revolutionary Guard for cyber attack on 700 retail sites
item.description: Paris will propose further sanctions against Iranian entities to its European partners. A Commission spokesperson said it is not the Commission's role to attribute cyber incidents. Iran rejects the accusations, and Paris prosecutors are seeking international arrest warrants.

item.title: Leo Batavus: EU auditors say uneven enforcement blunts Russia sanctions
item.description: Direct trade with Russia fell from 253 billion euros to 58 billion between 2021 and 2025. The European Court of Auditors calls for clearer rules and stronger monitoring, saying the Commission lacks criteria to judge whether the sanctions work.

item.title: The Harbour Ledger: EU sanctions cut Russia trade to 58 billion euros but enforcement lags
item.description: Trade fell from 253 billion euros in 2021. The European Court of Auditors says unclear rules and uneven application let firms bypass the bans, and Russia now trades more with India and China.

item.title: Europae Laeva: Up to 50 leaders join Rutte in Dublin in Garda's biggest operation, say Gardaí
item.description: More than 5,000 Gardaí will work over 15,000 twelve-hour tours for the summit, while protesters march on Friday over fuel prices and the cost of living.

item.title: Europa Patriarum: Portugal rebukes NATO chief Rutte over 'flippant' missile remarks
item.description: The foreign ministry in Lisbon objected to remarks suggesting the government downplays the Russian threat, as Spain stayed silent.

item.title: Attacotti: ESET links Cereal email malware found at Romanian agency to Russia-aligned Turla
item.description: The security firm says the toolset, run on Microsoft Exchange, was set up to collect emails involving NATO and EU addresses. A Kazakh government body was also compromised, and ESET reads that hit as surveillance of Russian dissidents.

item.title: Nuntii Europae: Slovak security firm links new email espionage tool to Russian hacking group Turla
item.description: ESET says the tool, found on a compromised Exchange server at a governmental organisation in Romania, was set to flag NATO and EU email traffic. A second victim in Kazakhstan was also identified.

item.title: The Harbour Ledger: Launch the Black Sea mission while Turla sits in government mail
item.description: A toolset built to filter NATO and EU correspondence sat on a Romanian government server, and Romania has asked for exactly this mission. Europe's governments should launch it and pay for cyber defence of ports and shipping lanes inside it.

item.title: Attacotti: US soldier arrested in England on suspicion of spying for Russia
item.description: The 41-year-old was detained near Gloucester under the National Security Act 2023 and remains in custody at a London police station. The FBI director said the case involves allegations of espionage, which can carry a life sentence before an American military court.

item.title: The Harbour Ledger: French cyber agency blames Iran's Revolutionary Guard for shop fridge attack
item.description: The cyberattack forced refrigeration at about 700 retail sites into high temperatures and destroyed the stock. The agency will ask European partners for new sanctions on Iranian entities.

item.title: Nuntii Europae: US, Ukraine and Russia open first talks since February in Abu Dhabi
item.description: Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff mediate two days of talks on security guarantees and territory, while Russian officials keep European representatives out of the main negotiations.

item.title: The Harbour Ledger: Hackers hit freezers at 700 French supermarkets, Paris blames Iran
item.description: France's Cyber Crisis Coordination Centre named Iran's Shahid Kaveh cyber unit in a report on Monday. One German store owner says he threw away goods worth over 360,000 euros.
